examples.en: I think it is a bold idea, but it could reduce pollution and traffic significantly.

examples.en: Public transport would have to improve first. Our buses are rarely reliable.

examples.en: And the fares are expensive for families with several children.

examples.en: Cars are so convenient, though. I can go anywhere whenever I want.

examples.target: まず公共交通を改善しないと。うちのバスは、めったに信頼できるものじゃないからね。
examples.en: Public transport would have to improve first. Our buses are rarely reliable.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: 市が中心部での車の通行を禁止しようとしているよ。どう思う？
dialogue.en: Our city wants to ban cars from the center. What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: 大胆な案だと思うけど、汚染と渋滞をかなり減らせるかもしれないね。
dialogue.en: I think it is a bold idea, but it could reduce pollution and traffic significantly.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: でも、配達の運転手みたいに車に頼っている人たちはどうなるの？
dialogue.en: But what about people who depend on their cars, like delivery drivers?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: 特別な許可証を出せば、地元の店を傷つけずに済むと思うよ。
dialogue.en: They could receive special permits, so the plan would not hurt local businesses.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: まず公共交通を改善しないと。うちのバスは、めったに信頼できるものじゃないからね。
dialogue.en: Public transport would have to improve first. Our buses are rarely reliable.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: その通り。頻繁で時間通りの運行がなければ、計画は失敗するよ。
dialogue.en: Exactly. Without frequent and punctual services, the plan will fail.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: それに、子どもが何人もいる家庭には運賃が高いよ。
dialogue.en: And the fares are expensive for families with several children.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: もっと安い定期券があれば、車を家に置いておく人が増えるかもね。
dialogue.en: A cheaper monthly pass would encourage more people to leave their cars at home.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: でも車は便利だよ。いつでもどこでも行けるから。
dialogue.en: Cars are so convenient, though. I can go anywhere whenever I want.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: 便利だけど、渋滞で時間を失うし、駐車場にもお金がかかるよね。
dialogue.en: Convenient, yes, but you also lose time in traffic and spend a lot on parking.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: それは本当だね。毎日、駐車スペースを探すのにほぼ一時間もかかっているよ。
dialogue.en: That is true. I spend nearly an hour a day looking for a place to park.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: 自転車専用道がうまく機能している都市もあるよ。
dialogue.en: Some cities show that cycling lanes can work very well.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: そうかもしれないけど、うちの冬は彼らのところより厳しいから。
dialogue.en: Perhaps, but our winters are harsher than theirs.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: なるほど、だから複数の解決策を組み合わせる必要があるんだろうね。
dialogue.en: Fair enough, which is why a mix of solutions is probably necessary.

dialogue.speaker: Ren
dialogue.text: 電車やバスが改善されるなら、その計画を支持してもいいかな。
dialogue.en: I might support the plan if the trains and buses improve.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: それが正しい条件だね。人々に代わりの手段があれば、変化はうまくいくよ。
dialogue.en: That would be the right condition. Change works best when people have alternatives.
